title: Total sets in quantum field theory
version: Reports on Mathematical Physics 2 (1971) 113-120; bibliographic data confirmed through the Crossref API
locator: Abstract only, and only as paraphrased in a web-search summary; the ScienceDirect page returned HTTP 403
assumptions: Not verified. The abstract as summarised states no mass hypothesis; Buchholz-Roberts attach a mass gap to its Theorem 2.
conclusion: As summarised: for a class of 'total' sets the Haag algebra equals that of all Minkowski space; the open past light cone and the 'open isotropic tube' are total; Araki's and Borchers' conditions do not give this.
relevance: The primary source for the massive cone result.
open_questions: Exact hypotheses of Theorem 2; free field only or any theory with a gap; meaning of 'isotropic tube'.
limits: Not openly accessible. No quotation from it is used as verified.

title: New Light on Infrared Problems: Sectors, Statistics, Symmetries and Spectrum
version: arXiv:1304.2794v4, 24 October 2013; published Commun. Math. Phys. 330 (2014) 935-972, not compared
locator: Sec. 1 (pp. 3-5); Sec. 3, Def. 3.1, Prop. 3.2 and the paragraph after it (p. 10); Sec. 8 (pp. 35-36); reference [24]. Pages 1, 3-5, 7-8, 10, 13-14, 33, 35-36, 44, 46 read through a page extraction
assumptions: Local net on a forward light cone in four dimensions with a vacuum state; extended net on Minkowski space.
conclusion: Authors' statements: R(V) is either B(H) or a type III_1 factor (citing Longo 1979, Rem. 4); B(H) if the spectrum has a mass gap, citing Sadowski-Woronowicz Thm 2; type III_1 with massless particles, by Huygens' principle, citing Buchholz 1977 p. 161.
proof_status: Stated with citations, not proved in this paper.
relevance: Precise statement of the massive result with its attribution and theorem number as cited by these authors.
open_questions: Whether Thm 2 of the 1971 paper is stated for general nets with a gap.
limits: Not all pages read. The theorem number is theirs, not checked.

title: Arrow of time and quantum physics
version: arXiv:2305.11709v1, 19 May 2023, 18 pages; pages 1-2 and 4-18 read through a page extraction
locator: Sec. 2, Prop. 2.1; Sec. 3, Lemma 3.1, cases (a)-(c), Prop. 3.2; Sec. 4, eq. (4.6)
assumptions: Net of light-cone C*-algebras with an endomorphic action of future timelike translations and a vacuum state; local subnet; unique invariant vector after central decomposition.
conclusion: Authors' results: if the extension of time translations to the past is not unique (equivalently R(V) is not B(H)), the spectrum is the whole closed forward cone. With a gap, R(V)=B(H) and all light-cone algebras coincide (credited to Sadowski-Woronowicz). With massless particles R(V) commutes with outgoing fields created in the past cone.
proof_status: Proof of Lemma 3.1 and Prop. 3.2 read. It relies on Borchers' theorem on half-sided translations (Borchers 1992; Florig 1998), not read.
dependencies: Borchers 1992; Florig 1998; Sakai Thm 2.4.3; Buchholz 1977, 1982 (none read).
relevance: An independent proof route for the massive verdict, read in full.
limits: The final step from 'vacuum projection in R(V)' to R(V)=B(H) is asserted there and written out by this session.

title: On the local structure of the Klein-Gordon field on curved spacetimes
version: arXiv:math-ph/0008043v2, 25 February 2001, 17 pages; published Lett. Math. Phys. 54 (2000) 249-261, not compared
locator: Sec. 2.3-2.4 (envelope; Prop. 2.1); Theorem 3.2; Prop. 4.1; Theorem 5.1; Cor. 5.3; Example 5.4
assumptions: Globally hyperbolic spacetime with metric locally analytic in time; real scalar field of mass m >= 0; continuous quasifree state.
conclusion: Author's results: a distributional solution vanishing on an open set vanishes on its envelope; the von Neumann algebra of an open set equals that of its envelope; the algebra of a timelike curve segment is that of the double cone it spans.
proof_status: Proofs read. They rest on unique-continuation theorems of Tataru and Hoermander, not read.
relevance: Supplies both the quantum and the classical thin-tube step for the free field of any mass.
limits: Minkowski spacetime is a special case; nothing about cones is said in the paper itself.

title: The Timelike Tube Theorem in Curved Spacetime
version: arXiv:2303.16380v1, 29 March 2023; pages 1-5, 10-16, 18-19 read through a page extraction
assumptions: Real analytic globally hyperbolic spacetime; additive algebras; dense set of analytic states.
conclusion: Authors' statement: A(U)=A(E(U)) for not necessarily free theories; originally Borchers 1961 and Araki 1963 in Minkowski space.
proof_status: Informal account of the proof in arXiv:2302.02709, which was not read.
relevance: Extends the thin-tube step beyond free fields. Says nothing about massive cone algebras.
limits: Pages 6-9 and 17 not read. The paper does not mention Sadowski-Woronowicz or the mass dependence of cone algebras.

title: Algebras, Regions, and Observers
version: arXiv:2303.02837v2, 26 April 2023; pages 1-3, 7-9, 11, 14-17, 23-24 read through a page extraction
locator: Sec. 3.1 (envelope of finite, infinite or semi-infinite timelike curves; Holmgren); Sec. 3.3 (massless free field in even dimension: commutator on the light cone, timelike-separated sets commute)
assumptions: Quantum field theory without gravity on a real analytic spacetime.
conclusion: Author's statements: the algebra of a thickened timelike curve depends only on the curve and equals that of its envelope; for a massless free field in even dimension D the algebras of regions joined by no null geodesic commute.
relevance: Semi-infinite worldlines and the massless contrast.
limits: Not all pages read. No statement about massive cone algebras was found in the pages read.
